title: Hospital & Unit Logistics
items: Layout & Key Depts: ED is on the 1st floor, ICU and med/surg on 3rd, OR on 2nd. Radiology and lab are on the ground floor.
Parking & Access: Staff park in Lot C. Badges are issued in the HR office. Scrubs are provided for procedures only.
Workroom: Yes, the hospitalist team has a dedicated room on the 3rd floor with workstations and a whiteboard.
Census: Daytime census is ~15 patients per hospitalist, 6–8 admissions/night.
Shifts: Days: 7a–7p. Nights: 7p–7a. Handoff occurs at the hospitalist room at 6:45.
Admin Contacts: IT Helpdesk: ext. 5555; HR: ext. 4010; Badge Office: ext. 4102.

title: EMR / Documentation
items: EMR System: Epic. Training provided during orientation week.
Dictation Tools: Yes, Dragon Medical One is available on all workstations.
Turnaround Time: Progress notes by end of shift; discharge summaries within 24 hours of discharge.
Discharge Summaries: Required for all discharges; Epic smart phrases available.
Note Format: Preferred format is APSO. Dot phrases provided in orientation packet.
Templates: .hospProgressNote, .dischargePlan, and .handoffSummary are commonly used.

title: Admissions & Consults
items: Admissions Assigned: Admitting hospitalist takes admissions via a rotational schedule.
From ED: Hospitalists admit all medical patients directly from the ED.
Direct Admissions: Yes, via a transfer center or outpatient referring MD; hospitalist confirms case before bed is assigned.
Specialty Consults: Order in Epic and page consult service. For urgent cases, call directly.
Co-management: Yes, ortho, psych, and neurosurg patients are co-managed with hospitalists.

title: ICU and Higher Level of Care
items: ICU Management: Closed ICU. Intensivist covers all ICU patients; hospitalists do not round there.
ICU Criteria: Based on vitals/labs/organ failure (e.g., sepsis, resp. failure). ICU team makes final call.
Rapid Response Protocol: Call ext. 9999 for RRT; staffed 24/7 by ICU nurse, RT, and on-call physician.
Code Blue Response: Hospitalists respond to codes only if they're the primary physician or on RRT call.

title: Orders & Protocols
items: Order Sets: Yes — standardized order sets for sepsis, CHF, COPD, and DKA.
Special Orders: Code status must be discussed with patient/family and documented. Restraint orders must be renewed every 24 hours.
Antibiotic Policy: Restricted antibiotics (e.g., meropenem, linezolid) require ID approval.
Anticoagulation/VTE: Pharmacy and nursing-led protocols; hospitalist must order based on risk.

title: Communication & Handoffs
items: Handoff Tool: I-PASS template used in Epic and reviewed verbally at shift change.
Team Contacts: Use PerfectServe for direct secure messaging; all disciplines available 24/7.
Rounds: Interdisciplinary rounds at 9 a.m. daily with case manager, pharmacist, and bedside nurse.
After-Hours: Covered by dedicated nocturnist. Cross-cover info included in handoff note.

title: Support Services
items: Case Management: Each floor has assigned CM and SW. Available M–F, 8a–5p.
Discharge Planning: CM initiates DME/SNF requests. Follow-up scheduled in Epic discharge navigator.
Home Health: Ordered in Epic; case manager will process and confirm agency.
Palliative Care: Available Mon–Sat; place Epic consult or page directly for urgent needs.
Spiritual Care: Chaplain available 7a–5p, on-call after hours via paging operator.

title: Scheduling & Coverage
items: Schedule Model: 7-on/7-off; one nocturnist, 4 day hospitalists per shift.
Schedule Requests: Submit to scheduler (Sandra J., ext. 4530) at least 1 month in advance.
Leave Policy: CME: 5 days/year; PTO: 20 days/year; notify group leader for coverage.
Extra Shifts: Available at $200/hour. Email group lead for open shifts.

title: Labs, Imaging, Ancillary
items: Turnaround Times: CBC/CMP ~1 hour; blood cultures ~48 hrs; CT within 2 hrs.
Urgent Studies: Call radiology reading room for stat CT/MRI prioritization.
Radiology Hours: In-house from 7a–11p; teleradiology overnight.
Critical Results: Called directly to ordering physician or covering provider.

title: Onboarding & Growth
items: Onboarding: 3-day orientation + shadow shifts. Training on EMR, workflows, protocols.
Mentorship: Assigned a senior hospitalist mentor for the first 3 months.
Performance Reviews: Done quarterly with metrics (LOS, readmissions, documentation).
Growth Opportunities: Openings in QI committee, sepsis task force, and medical staff leadership.
CME Support: $2,500/year CME allowance + 5 CME days.

title: Culture & Team Dynamics
items: Interdepartmental Relations: Strong collaboration with ED and case management. Some delays with ortho consults.
Common Workflow Challenges: Discharge delays due to transport/SNF placement. Radiology bottlenecks during evenings.
Advice for Success: Be proactive with discharge planning, document thoroughly, and use your team — case managers are your best resource.
